name: Red Paper-cut
summary: Folk window-flower paper-cuts that come alive: China-red cut-outs with hand-cut edges, inset double outlines and soft paper shadows on rice paper or indigo night paper; rosettes fold and snap open, letters pop in on 12 fps steps, captions sit on serrated swallow-tail banners, and gold foil arrives once, at the end.
suits: one thing becomes many (fold, cut, unfold)
facts told as a small ceremony

palette.use: rice paper: the day ground and the title paper
China red: the hero paper, cut letters, rosettes
the banner strip under captions and labels (darker than picture reds)
pale-red far layer on day grounds
gold foil: one late moment only (flecks on the end card)
indigo night paper: the second ground family
one step deeper red: printed small credits, heavy pieces
one step brighter red: near pieces
darker red: far pieces, stacked folded edges
the back of a flap past 90° while it folds
text on banners; cream cut letters on night paper
night sky at the top of a night ground
night far hills
night near hills; the blue strip
night houses
pale indigo paper: scattered light, snow
day mid layer
backlight centre (the lit window behind a rosette)
backlight middle; lit windows
backlight edge
a backlit rosette's red
paper shadow under every piece, at 38%

type.case: cut titles in capitals; banners and headlines in sentence case
type.emphasis: paper material: the emphasised words are knocked out of a red banner (yin cut); never a colour change in text

banned: painting, gradient shading or outline strokes (the backlight behind a lit rosette is the one exception)
shadow-puppet looks: no light behind a screen, no translucent hide, no rods
flat vector art without cut edges, rims and paper shadows
a silhouette film: every shape's interior is cut
perspective depth: layers stay parallel to the screen
dissolves and fades: paper folds, peels, drops or is cut
smoothed architecture; floating islands in a cut; morphing faces
a red hero on a red ground; gold as a second main colour
copying named artists' cuts, studio characters or real motif sheets
film grain (the paper fibres are the texture)
